$comment: This file is the resource library. Edit it to add or remove a PDF or an external link. Guides are NOT listed here - they are markdown files in content/guides/ and get picked up automatically. See README.md for the full instructions.

categories.label: TrueLoad Guides
categories.blurb: How to use TrueLoad itself — setup, utility data, and producing a report.

categories.label: Code & Standards
categories.blurb: What the code actually requires — the primary sources themselves, plus plain-language explanations of them.

categories.label: Utility Data
categories.blurb: Getting interval data out of a utility, and knowing what you are looking at once you have it.

categories.label: Research & Studies
categories.blurb: Independent work on panel capacity, electrification, and what upgrades actually cost.

resources.title: Understanding NEC 220.87
resources.description: A two-page plain-language guide: what 220.87 permits, how a measured-demand calculation differs from the traditional method, and the LBNL research behind it. Written for contractors, homeowners and inspectors alike.

resources.title: TrueLoad User Guide
resources.description: The complete walkthrough: setting up a project, requesting utility data, entering new load, and producing the report you hand to the AHJ.

resources.title: NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code) — free online access
resources.description: The code itself, readable in full at no cost. NFPA publishes every edition of NFPA 70 for free online viewing. Article 220.87 is the section TrueLoad implements.

resources.title: The Green Button standard
resources.description: The industry-standard format for utility usage data. If your utility offers "Download My Data", this is what you are getting and what it contains.

resources.title: Green Button Download My Data (DMD)
resources.description: How the customer-initiated download works, and which utilities have been certified to provide it.

resources.title: Sizing Electric Service Panels and Utility Infrastructure
resources.description: LBNL technical brief on how service panels have historically been sized, and why the assumptions behind that sizing no longer match how homes actually use electricity.

resources.title: Reducing the Cost of Electrification with Alternatives to Electric Panel Upgrades
resources.description: A survey of the options available when a panel looks undersized on paper — including establishing actual measured demand before assuming an upgrade is required.

resources.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Electrical Panel Capacities in U.S. Single-Family Homes
resources.description: ACEEE study quantifying how much of the existing housing stock is genuinely capacity-constrained versus how much only appears to be under a worst-case calculation.

resources.title: Residential Electrification Under Electrical Panel and Service Constraints
resources.description: US Department of Energy overview of the panel-constraint problem and the research program addressing it. Good orientation if you are new to the topic.
